definition: Unverified means not yet checked or confirmed as true.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word unverified. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know unverified should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The class wiki shades every unverified figure yellow until an editor traces it to a source.
Unsubstantiated goes further than unverified: an unverified claim simply hasn't been checked yet, while an unsubstantiated one has been shopped around and no support has turned up.
Discredited is the far end: the unverified claim awaits its test, the unsubstantiated claim lacks support, and the discredited claim took the test and failed it.

Unconfirmed means no authority has yet said yes: the announcement, the official word, the sign-off has not come. Unverified points at the checking itself — nobody has yet tested the claim against records, witnesses, or sources. A report can be unconfirmed simply because the confirming call never happened.

Untested describes something never yet put through a trial — a rookie goalie, a new engine design, a theory awaiting its first experiment. Unverified is narrower and belongs to claims: a statement nobody has yet checked against records or sources. Things go untested; assertions go unverified.

Unverified means not yet checked or confirmed as true.
Family legend says Great-Grandpa pitched an inning against a touring big-league team in 1934.
The story is unverified - no scorecard, no clipping, no roster - which is not the same as false; it waits, patiently, for somebody to check the county archive.
Unverified is precise because it passes no judgment either way: the story may be perfectly true - it simply has not been checked against anything.
The moment someone finds the 1934 scorecard, it graduates to verified; if the archive shows the team never toured, it falls apart.
Unverified takes no side at all: the checking has not happened, so belief should wait.
The moment doubt sets in, the word is dubious (this unit); if support was sought and none found, unsubstantiated.
And it applies to claims, not plans - a changeable schedule is tentative, not unverified.

Every line of it is, for now, unverified.
